data.summary: Added a STALE problem code with a `Problem.stale(inputIndex, requestId, maxAgeDays)` factory whose message quotes the configured threshold, and gave WorkRequestValidator an optional `(Clock, Duration)` constructor that rejects requests strictly older than maxAge inside the existing validate stage (counted out of the trace, noted as "<id> rejected: stale", never passed to deduplication); the no-arg constructor leaves staleness checking off. Added `StalenessProperties` bound from `app.staleness` with a `30d` default and a positivity check, and wired a UTC `Clock` bean plus the clock-backed validator in ProcessingConfig.
uncertainties: OrderIndependenceTest.generatedBatchCoversEveryKindOfProblem asserts every ProblemCode appears in a generated batch; I could not see that file, so its generator may need a stale request added (and a clock-backed validator) to keep covering the new STALE code — the separately written tests presumably handle this.
I left src/main/resources/application.yml untouched (contents not shown); the 30d default comes from @DefaultValue, so no property entry is required.

StalenessProperties throws NullPointerException (not IllegalArgumentException) for a null maxAge, since @DefaultValue means binding never yields null; only the non-positive case is spelled out in the criteria.
Problem.stale uses the existing subject(requestId) helper, so a null requestId would read "Request is older than N days"; for the specified non-null case the message matches exactly.
